_about: Product criticality judgment for every workflow in the corpus. This is a judgment, not research evidence, which is why it lives beside dedupe-decisions.json and NOT inside docs/research/raw/ - those files are primary-source vendor evidence, and criticality is sourced from no vendor. The corpus discipline is that an unsourced claim gets labelled; this one is unsourced by nature.
_not_stored_here: Whether a workflow is BUILT is deliberately absent. It is measurable from git and from the feature registry, and storing derived state here would recreate the stale-dashboard bug that make_status.py exists to prevent. Join against the host, do not cache it.
_consumed_by: tools/build_corpus.py, which is the only place ticket ids are assigned. Regenerating INDEX.md and workflows.json fails non-zero if a ticket is missing here or if an entry names a ticket that does not exist.

criteria.critical: Remove it and you no longer have a usable digital sales room. Qualifies via any one of C1, C2, C3.
criteria.supplementary: The primary loop closes without it. It adds reach, automation, polish, or adjacent product surface.
criteria.C1: Primary path - sits on the irreducible loop: create a room, put content in, give a buyer access, buyer consumes it, seller learns what happened.
criteria.C2: Trust precondition - you cannot put real confidential material in front of real buyers without it.
criteria.C3: Enabler - other workflows physically cannot function without it.

_contested: WF-132: called supplementary because the loop closes without in-room comments. The counter-argument is strong: a room you cannot talk inside is a tracked link, not a room. This is the most contestable call in the file.

The whole crm-integration domain: true that a DSR works without a CRM, false that an enterprise sales team adopts one. Adoption-critical without being product-critical. The test was kept clean rather than letting go-to-market pressure inflate the set.
WF-009: supplementary for a single seller who publishes directly, critical for a regulated team that cannot ship content ungated.
WF-017: supplementary for a product team, critical for an agency reselling under client brands.
_conditional: WF-082 becomes critical the moment inbound ingestion (WF-113/WF-114) ships: accepting external webhooks without signature verification and IP allowlisting is a live security hole rather than a missing feature.
WF-085 is a hard legal gate for any EU customer even though it is not a loop requirement. It blocks selling, not using.

decisions.rationale: There is no room without it, and nothing downstream has anything to attach to.
How content reaches the buyer's eyes; without page assembly the room has no buyer-facing surface.
The library is the substance of a room. An empty room is not a sales room.
Granting a specific buyer access with a role is the act that makes the room a shared space rather than a draft.
Lifecycle hygiene. Dealing closes without archiving; this keeps the workspace tidy afterwards.
The 'seller learns what happened' stage. This is the single reason a DSR beats a folder of PDFs, and the whole analytics-intent domain layers on top of it.
Content has to enter the system somehow; WF-003 governs a library that this fills.
Convenience ingest path. WF-007 already gets a document into the library; this only keeps it current automatically.
Approval gating is a team-governance overlay. A lone seller publishes directly. Contested for regulated teams.
Findability at scale. With a small library you scroll; the loop never depended on search.
Publish and hand over the link. Without this the room exists but nobody outside can ever see it.
Automates WF-001. Volume convenience, not a capability the loop lacks.
Personalisation improves conversion; a static room still functions.
Being unable to end access means every link is permanent. Confidential material cannot be shared on that basis.
Without any check on who the buyer is, 'restrict to this deal' is unenforceable and the audit trail attributes actions to nobody.
Pushes events outward. The room works standalone; this is adoption surface for CRM-centric teams.
Branding. Commercially important to resellers, absent from the primary loop.
Depth on top of WF-006. Per-page resolution refines visibility that already exists at document level.
Attribution analytics for content strategy; a seller can act on WF-006 without it.
BI export surface. Useful to a data team, not to the deal in front of the seller.
A derived label over observed engagement. Interpretation, not capability.
Portfolio triage convenience once you have many rooms.
Correlational reporting across two systems; depends on CRM integration that is itself supplementary.
Management roll-up. Multi-threading insight, not a loop requirement.
Outbound webhook delivery to the customer's own systems. Note the name: it is server-to-server push, not a live client feed.
Mirrors events into a CRM activity timeline. Convenience of review, not a capability.
Interpretation layer over engagement events.
Automation on top of WF-027; a human can act on the signal directly.
Feeds DSR activity into CRM lead scoring. Wholly dependent on CRM integration.
Triggering external CRM workflows is downstream integration, not the room itself.
Anonymous-visitor de-anonymisation. A marketing capability adjacent to the sales room.
Outbound intent delivery to external systems, same shape as WF-025.
Account-list maintenance driven by intent data. Adjacent product.
Entry point of the CRM cluster. Adoption-critical for enterprise buyers, absent from the product loop.
Field mapping detail beneath WF-034.
Provisioning CRM-side schema; only meaningful once the connector exists.
Single-event logging into an external system.
Sync efficiency and idempotency, not a room capability.

The buyer link is public by construction. Password, expiry and email verification are what stop a forwarded link becoming a leak.
NDA gating is situational; many deals never require one.
Watermarking is a deterrent and a trace, not an access control.
Download restriction hardens sharing that already works.
Screenshot blocking is largely unenforceable from a browser; treat as deterrence, and do not sell it as protection.
Per-item scoping for large organisations. WF-004's roles carry the basic case.
Engagement review; analytics on access rather than access itself.
Early revocation is the difference between a mistake and an incident. Keeping the audit row is what makes it defensible afterwards.
Without internal roles every user is an admin, so there is no answer to 'who was allowed to do this'. Also a C3 enabler: permission checks have nothing to check against until roles exist.
Signer identity verification belongs to the e-signature cluster.
The audit trail is the product's central claim. While it can only be read inside the process that wrote it, the guarantee is unfalsifiable to any outsider.
